response_text:
Summary
To achieve a creamy vegan mushroom risotto without dairy, this recipe leverages the high amylopectin starch content of Arborio rice combined with a technique called "mantecatura" (vigorous whipping off the heat). By introducing cold vegan butter and nutritional yeast at the very end, you create a rich emulsion that mimics the texture of parmesan cheese. The addition of soy sauce or miso provides the necessary savory umami depth often missing in vegetable-based broths.

Assumptions
I assume you have a heavy-bottomed pot (like a Dutch oven) to maintain consistent heat and a ladle for gradual liquid addition.

Structured Details
**Ingredients (Serves 4)**
| Ingredient | Quantity | Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Arborio Rice | 1.5 cups | Do not rinse (preserves starch) |
| Vegetable Broth | 5-6 cups | Keep hot in a separate pot |
| Mixed Mushrooms | 1 lb | Cremini, Shiitake, or Oyster; sliced |
| Dry White Wine | 1/2 cup | Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio |
| Shallot | 1 large | Finely diced (or small yellow onion) |
| Nutritional Yeast | 3 tbsp | Provides "cheesy" flavor |
| Vegan Butter | 2 tbsp | Cold, cubed (for finishing) |
| Soy Sauce/Miso | 1 tbsp | Umami booster |

**Cooking Procedure**
Phase 1: Base & Toast | Build flavor foundation | High Heat
Heat olive oil in your heavy pot. Sauté the sliced mushrooms until browned and their liquid has evaporated (approx 8 mins). Remove mushrooms and set aside. Reduce heat to medium, add diced shallot to the same pot. Cook until translucent. Add the Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes until grain edges are translucent but centers are white.
Action: [Button: Rice Toasting Visuals] https://www.google.com/search?q=risotto+rice+toasted+visual

Phase 2: Deglaze & Absorption | Release starch slowly | Medium Heat
Pour in the white wine and stir constantly until fully evaporated. Begin adding the hot vegetable broth one ladle (approx 1/2 cup) at a time. Stir frequently to agitate the rice grains against each other—this releases the starch. Wait until the liquid is mostly absorbed before adding the next ladle. Repeat for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente.
Action: [Button: Stirring Technique] https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=risotto+stirring+technique

Phase 3: The Mantecatura | Create emulsion | Heat Off
Remove the pot from the heat immediately. This is crucial. Stir in the cooked mushrooms, nutritional yeast, soy sauce (or miso), and the cold vegan butter. Whip the mixture vigorously with a wooden spoon for 60 seconds. The agitation combines the starch and fat into a glossy, creamy sauce.
Action: [Button: Vegan Butter Brands] https://www.google.com/search?q=best+vegan+butter+for+cooking

Phase 4: Plating | Serve immediately | Warm
Check seasoning and add salt/pepper. The consistency should be "all'onda" (wavy)—it should flow slowly when the plate is tilted, not stand stiff like mashed potatoes. Garnish with fresh parsley or thyme.
Action: [Button: Plating Ideas] https://www.google.com/search?q=gourmet+risotto+plating+ideas

# Summary
This 3-day itinerary for April 5–7, 2024, is optimized for a family with children (ages 8 and 10) during Kyoto's peak cherry blossom season. The plan prioritizes direct transit and strategic taxi use to adhere to the 30-minute walking limit, balancing historical "must-sees" with active nature stops and kid-approved dining.

# Assumptions
- **Base:** Staying near Kyoto Station for optimal access to JR and subway lines.
- **Transit:** Primary travel via train/subway; taxis recommended for steep temple approaches (e.g., Kiyomizu-dera) to conserve energy.
- **Pacing:** Morning activity + lunch + Afternoon activity format to prevent fatigue.

# Structured Details

Option 1: Day 1 - 10,000 Gates & Old Kyoto
**Southern Higashiyama** | **Fushimi Inari & Kiyomizu-dera** | **Hiking & Views**
Take the JR Nara Line to Inari Station (5 min ride). The shrine entrance is directly opposite. Hike the "Senbon Torii" gates to the Yotsutsuji intersection (approx. 30-40 min round trip) for views without the full mountain climb. For lunch, try Kitsune Udon (fox noodles) near the station. In the afternoon, take a taxi (approx. 15 min, ~1500 JPY) directly to the Kiyomizu-dera entrance to avoid the steep uphill walk. Walk downhill through Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka streets to see traditional shops.
Action: [Button: Fushimi Inari Guide] https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3915.html

Option 2: Day 2 - Bamboo Forest & Monkey Park
**Arashiyama District** | **Bamboo Grove & Iwatayama** | **Nature & Animals**
Take the JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama Station (15 min ride). Walk 10 minutes to the famous Bamboo Grove. Visit Tenryu-ji temple nearby if time permits. Cross the Togetsukyo Bridge to the Monkey Park entrance. The hike up is steep but short (approx. 20 mins); kids can feed wild macaques safely from a hut at the top. Return to the river area for matcha soft-serve ice cream.
Action: [Button: Monkey Park Info] http://www.monkeypark.jp/

Option 3: Day 3 - Golden Pavilion & Food Adventure
**North & Central** | **Kinkaku-ji & Nishiki Market** | **Iconic & Tasty**
Take a taxi (20 mins) or City Bus 205 to Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) right at 9:00 AM opening to beat crowds. The walking path here is flat and takes about 45 minutes. Transit to Shijo Station (Subway Karasuma Line) for lunch at Nishiki Market. This "Kitchen of Kyoto" offers kid-friendly skewers, tamagoyaki (egg rolls), and sweets. End the day at the Pokemon Center Kyoto (Suina Muromachi building, 5 min walk from market).
Action: [Button: Nishiki Market Map] https://www.kyoto-nishiki.or.jp/

Bangkok is in its peak dry season, characterized by bright blue skies, plenty of sunshine, and warm temperatures that can get hot in the afternoon. Hanoi, located further north, is in the middle of its winter, bringing cool to cold temperatures, persistent grey skies, and high humidity often accompanied by a light misty drizzle.
